analysis: The PR changes only docs/provider/cli-reference.md: the 'Last updated' date plus one new row (head line 572 per patch hunk) documenting a `--prompt-prep` benchmark mode (CPU-only, tokenizer-only, prints JSON, exits 2 on token-ID or decoded-field differences). The base and head excerpts supplied cover other regions of the same doc, which I read as unchanged surrounding context. I found no changes to code, config defaults, trust-boundary behavior, attestation, authorization, encryption, cache gating (T-041) or the provider/coordinator wire contract (TB-002, TB-011). The documented cache, App Attest, logout, fan and report statements are unchanged and do not alter any security control. The new row documents a benchmark that loads only the tokenizer. It does not claim any new network, key or plaintext handling, so no new attack surface is evident from the doc. The one unverified item is that the PromptPreparationBenchmark.swift implementation was not supplied. If the benchmark prints prompt text or decoded bodies in its JSON output, that could expose plaintext locally. The doc says it uses synthetic conversations of given lengths and gives no sign of consumer data. Because the implementation is outside the supplied evidence, this is recorded as a coverage limit, not a finding. No threat-model updates are needed from this doc-only change.
